passage:
Anna lost her red scarf on the bus. It was not expensive, but it was important to her because her grandmother made it.
She called the bus company, but no one had found it. She checked the school office, the classroom, and even the playground. The scarf was gone.
Three days later, Anna saw a little girl wearing a red scarf at the bus stop. Anna looked carefully and saw a small blue flower on one end. It was her scarf.
The girl's mother explained that they had found it on the bus and planned to take it to the lost-and-found office. Anna thanked them and smiled.
The scarf returned with a small lesson: not every lost thing is stolen. Some things are simply waiting for the right person to bring them back.
